Just a heads up to folks to be careful what you buy.

First thing is to confirm that what you are trying to buy actually exists. For example, anything being sold as a German coin with the likeness of Hitler on it is fake. They don't exist in the real world as real coins of Germany. Standard issue Reichsmarks of the Third Reich mostly had Paul Von Hindenburg or just an eagle on them (Martin Luther, a church, and Schiller also appeared). Coins of Russia and the USSR also have many fantasy issues that are often listed as "commemorative" but are not real coins issued by anyone. Numista is a great source for determining if something decently modern even exists (before the 1600s you almost have to hit auction listings and other methods to determine if something is real).

Second, make sure if it does exist that yours is real. Chinese fakes of tons of coins exist, especially Chinese coins. If I had a dollar for every fake Chinese "dollar" (really tons of different denominations but all about dollar sized) and had to give 50 cents back for every real one I had seen I would still have enough to buy a couple of real ones. Weight and magnets are your friends. Fakes usually as either magnetic or weigh wrong. Those that match weight and are not magnetic usually have other issues (common in Morgan fakes, they have flat strikes or bad lettering or something similar).

Just be safe out there folks. Exonumia (non-coin items that people collect that are kind of related to coins) are cool if you know that is what you are getting but if you think you are getting the real thing they suck. I know folks who collect bad fakes just because they enjoy it. Collect what you want, but make sure it is what you want.
